verdict.rationale: React's own docs cover both halves of the story. For maintainability, it offers composable encapsulated components, TypeScript prop typing and eslint-plugin-react-hooks rules that catch severe bugs early. For performance, React Compiler memoizes automatically at build time and can be adopted incrementally across a codebase, and React DevTools identifies performance problems. Missing for 10: explicit first-party evidence about scaling with team size and codebase growth, and independent or hands-on corroboration of large-app performance.

support.subject: As a developer, I can build large applications that stay fast and maintainable as my team and codebase grow

citations.quote: Build encapsulated components that manage their own state, then compose them to make complex UIs.
React Compiler automatically optimizes your React application at build time
React Compiler can be adopted incrementally, allowing you to try it on specific parts of your codebase first.
Use React Developer Tools to inspect React components, edit props and state, and identify performance problems.
